label: janna, to know
note: Introduced by HI-C95-jaanta-hun and HI-C95-jaante-hain. The note is right and the defect is SHARPER than it states. It says the negation lesson's example sentence is `main nahiin jaantaa` so the learner meets the word while no atom introduces it. In fact jaantaa is in HI-C07-nahin's HEADWORD -- `nahiin / jaantaa` -- glossed as the masculine present form of to know, while all three of that lesson's atoms are about nahiin itself: its Sanskrit root, its Indo-European cousins, its two jobs. THE HEADWORD PROMISED A WORD THE ATOMS NEVER DELIVERED, so a learner could deny knowing something and not claim it. The affirmative needs no new grammar: take nahiin out and huun comes back, because a Hindi present needs its copula and the negative drops it. It did need a LETTER -- ja, which the corrected glyph check found had never been drawn either, and which HI-S132-letter-ja now teaches at chapter 30.
